title: US Government Suspends Access to Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5
description: The US government issued an export control directive to suspend all access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 by any foreign national. Anthropic stated the government believes there's a method of 'jailbreaking' the models, specifically around reading codebases and fixing software flaws. Simon verified his access was cut off at 6:59pm Pacific on June 12, 2026.
author: Simon Willison

title: OpenAI WebRTC Audio Session with Document Context
description: Simon updated his OpenAI WebRTC playground tool to support GPT-Realtime-2 (described as 'first voice model with GPT-5-class reasoning') and added ability to paste document context for audio conversations. The tool allows exploring information conversationally through audio interface.
author: Simon Willison

title: Claude Fable is Relentlessly Proactive
description: After two days with Claude Fable 5, Simon describes it as 'relentlessly proactive' - it knows many tricks and will deploy any of them to reach its goal. The post includes a detailed example of Fable jumping directly to a bug location without being asked to search first.
author: Simon Willison

title: Datasette 1.0a33 with JSON extras in the API
description: Simon released Datasette 1.0a33, extending the ?_extra= pattern to cover queries and rows. Because API explorer tools are 'almost free to build now', he had Claude Fable 5 (for planning) and GPT-5.5 xhigh in Codex Desktop (for implementation) build a custom extras API explorer to demonstrate the feature.
author: Simon Willison

title: asyncinject 0.7 - Bug Fixes by Claude Fable 5
description: Simon released asyncinject 0.7, a utility library for asyncio dependency injection. Claude Fable 5 spotted some bugs in the dependency which it then fixed for Simon. He notes 'It's a very proactive model!'
author: Simon Willison

title: Anthropic Walks Back Invisible Safeguards Policy
description: Anthropic reversed their policy of invisible safeguards for frontier LLM development in Fable/Mythos after widespread outrage. Wired reported on the policy that Claude would silently limit effectiveness for requests targeting frontier LLM development. Anthropic stated: 'We made the wrong tradeoff and we apologize for not getting the balance right.' Safeguards will now be visible.
author: Simon Willison

title: Datasette Agent 0.2a0 with User Interaction
description: Simon released datasette-agent 0.2a0 with major new feature: tools can now ask users questions mid-execution. The ask_user() feature was enabled by a new LLM alpha built with help from Claude Fable 5. Also includes new save_query tool that requires human approval.
author: Simon Willison

title: DiffusionGemma - Open Weight Model from Google
description: Simon highlighted Google's release of diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it as an open weight Apache 2 licensed model. NVIDIA is hosting it free on their NIM cloud API. Simon generated a pelican illustration at ~500 tokens/second. This brings back Google's experimental Gemini Diffusion research from last year.
author: Simon Willison

title: Jeremy Howard on AI Self-Improvement and Anthropic
description: Jeremy Howard shared thoughts on slowing recursive AI self-improvement, suggesting the top lab should not use their top model for frontier AI research but everyone else should have access. He criticized Anthropic for doing the opposite: allowing themselves to use their top model for frontier AI research while sabotaging others who try.
author: Simon Willison (quoting Jeremy Howard)

title: If Claude Fable Stops Helping You, You'll Never Know
description: Simon highlighted concerning details from Fable/Mythos 319-page system card: Anthropic implemented invisible interventions that limit Claude's effectiveness for requests targeting frontier LLM development (pretraining pipelines, distributed training infrastructure, ML accelerator design). Safeguards are not visible to user and use prompt modification, steering vectors, or PEFT. Update: Anthropic later walked back this policy.
author: Simon Willison

title: Initial Impressions of Claude Fable 5
description: After ~5.5 hours with Claude Fable 5, Simon calls it 'something of a beast' - slow, expensive, and happily churning through everything thrown at it. He notes the challenge is finding tasks it can't do. Comprehensive review of capabilities and performance.
author: Simon Willison

title: llm 0.32a3 - Almost Entirely Written by Claude Fable 5
description: Simon released llm 0.32a3, noting it was 'almost entirely written by the new Claude Fable 5'. This demonstrates the capability of AI coding agents to contribute meaningfully to open source projects.
author: Simon Willison

title: Andrej Karpathy on Jevons Paradox and AI-Generated Software
description: Andrej Karpathy shared thoughts on how 'working software increasingly comes out on a tap' and Jevons paradox kicks in - demand for software grows substantially. He mentions you can 'ask for anything - explainers, visualizers, dashboards, bespoke single-use apps' and '10X your test suite, auto-optimize code, run giant research projects'. Says 'Free your mind' (Matrix reference).
author: Andrej Karpathy (quoted by Simon Willison)

title: Datasette Agent Edit Plugin
description: Simon released datasette-agent-edit 0.1a0, a base plugin for agentic text editing. Implements view, str_replace, and insert tools inspired by Claude text editor design. This enables plugins for collaborative Markdown editing, updating SQL queries, and editing SVG files.
author: Simon Willison

title: Running Python Code in a Sandbox with MicroPython and WASM
description: Simon released micropython-wasm 0.1a2, his latest sandboxing experiment that bundles a WASM build of MicroPython with wasmtime wrapper. He's using it for a code execution sandbox plugin for Datasette Agent called datasette-agent-micropython. Notes that GPT-5.5 has so far failed to break out of the sandbox.
author: Simon Willison

title: Uber Caps Usage of AI Tools Like Claude Code to Manage Costs
description: Uber blew through its entire 2026 AI budget in just four months due to aggressive use of agentic coding tools like Claude Code. In response, Uber limited all employees to $1,500 in monthly token spending per AI coding tool. Power users were running 10+ parallel worktrees on Claude Code. Monthly costs per engineer ranged from $500 to $2,000. Simon notes this is a rational policy response, much more sensible than tokenmaxxing leaderboards.
author: Simon Willison

title: OpenAI Lockdown Mode - Preventing Data Exfiltration from Prompt Injection
description: Simon analyzed OpenAI's new Lockdown Mode feature, designed to prevent the final stage of data exfiltration from prompt injection attacks by limiting outbound network requests. He explains this directly attacks the exfiltration leg of the 'Lethal Trifecta' (private data + untrusted content + data exfiltration vectors). OpenAI CISO noted this is for users with elevated risk profiles. Simon notes the existence of lockdown mode implies ChatGPT defaults don't provide robust protection against data exfiltration attacks.
author: Simon Willison

title: AI Enthusiasts vs Skeptics: Race Against Time vs Entropy
description: Simon highlighted Charity Majors' analysis of the dynamic between AI enthusiasts and skeptics in software teams. Enthusiasts see 'discontinuous leaps in capabilities' and teams that sit this out 'could be out of business before the dust settles'. Skeptics note that when you 'ship code faster than engineers can read it', you make withdrawals from trust accounts, reliability degrades, and systems become incomprehensible. Charity notes 'There is no natural feedback loop connecting enthusiasts with skeptics' and designing feedback loops to 'mend the gap in shared reality' is a key organizational design problem.
author: Simon Willison (quoting Charity Majors)

title: Claude Fable 5: Mid-tier Results on Coding Tasks
description: Hacker News discussion comparing Claude Fable 5's performance on coding tasks. Key insights: Claude is described as 'a much better planner' while 'Codex is a much more professional coder.' Discussion notes you can 'mask a surprisingly amount of terrible coding with proper planning' and explores trade-offs between different AI coding assistants.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Claude Fable is Relentlessly Proactive - HN Discussion
description: Hacker News discussion on Simon Willison's observation about Claude Fable 5 being 'relentlessly proactive'. Critics noted that Claude models 'write too much unnecessary code, burn excessive tokens, and create unnecessary tests.' Community discussion about the trade-offs of aggressive AI assistance in development workflows.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Fable Refuses to do LLM-related Work
description: Hacker News discussion reporting that Claude Fable 5 refuses to help with developing LLMs or answering questions about LLM-related topics. This relates to Anthropic's invisible safeguards policy for frontier LLM development that was later walked back after community outrage.
author: Hacker News Community

title: What it Feels Like to Work with Mythos
description: Hacker News discussion about working with Claude Mythos 5. Key insight: AI creates 'inefficient code, but doing it at lightspeed with minimal effort,' resulting in unmaintainable code. Discussion explores the trade-offs between speed and maintainability when using AI coding assistants.
author: Hacker News Community

title: State of AI in 2026: LLMs, Coding, Scaling Laws, China, Agents, GPUs, AGI
description: Lex Fridman Podcast episode #490 featuring Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka discussing the comprehensive state of AI in 2026. Topics include LLMs and coding, scaling laws, AI agents, GPU developments, AGI progress, China's role in AI, programming and developer tooling, and open vs closed LLMs.
author: Lex Fridman with Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka
